title: Malignancy in childhood
objectives: Stage neuroblastoma (INRGSS) and Wilms and state what shifts risk.
Write the Wilms and hepatoblastoma operative sequence including nephron-sparing calls.
List chemotherapy classes with mechanism plus signature toxicity each.
body_md:
### Why this area matters

Oncology is Paper 1 territory: neuroblastoma, Wilms, hepatoblastoma, germ-cell tumours, rhabdomyosarcoma, plus the chemo-mechanism grid and febrile neutropenia protocol. Staging systems and risk stratification are the skeleton of every answer.

### Neuroblastoma and Wilms

Neuroblastoma: neural-crest origin, VMA/HVA, N-myc and segmental chromosomal changes, INRGSS stages (L1/L2 locoregional with/without image-defined risk factors, M metastatic, MS special infant pattern); surgery's role runs from biopsy through delayed resection after neoadjuvant therapy. Wilms: triphasic histology, favourable versus anaplastic, NWTS-style upfront-surgery versus SIOP-style neoadjuvant thinking, nephron-sparing for bilateral, syndromic or solitary-kidney disease; pulmonary metastases and IVC thrombus extend the workup.

### Liver, germ-cell and RMS

Hepatoblastoma: AFP tracking, PRETEXT staging, neoadjuvant chemotherapy then resection or transplant for unresectable disease. Germ-cell tumours: sacrococcygeal teratoma needs coccygectomy with the specimen; testicular tumours balance markers, orchidectomy approach (inguinal, cord control) and testis-preservation criteria. Rhabdomyosarcoma: embryonal versus alveolar biology, site-driven prognosis (orbit and non-bladder-prostate genitourinary fare better), multimodal therapy with function-preserving surgery.

### Chemotherapy and radiation

Alkylators (myelosuppression, infertility, second malignancy), anthracyclines (cumulative cardiotoxicity, dexrazoxane/echo surveillance), vinca alkaloids (neuropathy, constipation, extravasation necrosis), platinum agents (ototoxicity, nephrotoxicity, hydration protocols), antimetabolites (mucositis, hepatotoxicity). Radiation in children costs growth, fertility and second malignancies — proton therapy appears as the sparing advance. Febrile neutropenia protocol closes the answer (see module IV).

### How it is asked

Biology → staging → risk group → sequence of modalities → surgeon's exact role → follow-up. Never describe surgery without its neoadjuvant/adjuvant neighbours.
